facts.text: The README identifies the repository as example robots and code for interfacing Gazebo with ROS and states GPL-3.0 licensing.

The README's ROS Control quick start runs rrbot_control.launch and shows the position command rostopic pub /rrbot/joint2_position_controller/command std_msgs/Float64 with data -0.9; the value is an example, not a declared joint limit.
rrbot_control.yaml configures joint_state_controller as joint_state_controller/JointStateController with publish_rate 50.
rrbot_control.yaml configures joint1_position_controller for joint1 and joint2_position_controller for joint2 as effort_controllers/JointPositionController with PID gains 100.0, 0.01 and 10.0.

rrbot_control.launch loads rrbot_control.yaml and spawns joint_state_controller, joint1_position_controller and joint2_position_controller through the controller_manager spawner under the /rrbot namespace.
rrbot_control.launch remaps /joint_states to /rrbot/joint_states for robot_state_publisher.
The rqt publisher records /rrbot/joint1_position_controller/command with type_name std_msgs/Float64, enabled False, rate 100.0 and the data expression sin(i/100).
The rqt plot records /rrbot/joint1_position_controller/command/data and /rrbot/joint1_position_controller/state/error as field expressions.
rrbot_control/package.xml declares controller_manager, joint_state_controller, robot_state_publisher, rqt_gui and effort_controllers as runtime dependencies.
rrbot.xacro declares joint1 as a continuous joint with axis 0 1 0 and damping 0.7.
rrbot.xacro declares joint2 as a continuous joint with axis 0 1 0 and damping 0.7.
rrbot.xacro declares SimpleTransmission blocks for joint1 and joint2 that use hardware_interface/EffortJointInterface.
rrbot.gazebo loads libgazebo_ros_control.so with robotNamespace /rrbot and gazebo_ros_control/DefaultRobotHWSim.
rrbot_world.launch exposes a paused launch argument defaulting to false and forwards it to gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with the rrbot world.
rrbot_world.launch starts gazebo_ros spawn_model to spawn the robot_description URDF as model rrbot.
The gazebo_tutorials world plugin requires libgazebo_ros_api_plugin.so from the gazebo_ros package to be loaded.
The Hokuyo sensor plugin declares the topic /rrbot/laser/scan; this fact records the topic, not a message type.
The camera plugin declares cameraName rrbot/camera1 and imageTopicName image_raw, giving the topic /rrbot/camera1/image_raw; this fact records the topic, not a message type.
The RViz configuration displays /rrbot/laser/scan as a rviz/LaserScan display.
The RViz configuration displays /rrbot/camera1/image_raw as a rviz/Camera display.
rrbot_control/package.xml declares the licence BSD.
rrbot_description/package.xml declares the licence BSD.
rrbot_gazebo/package.xml declares the licence BSD.
gazebo_tutorials/package.xml declares the licence TODO.
rrbot_rqt.launch starts rqt_gui with the rrbot_rqt.perspective file.
rrbot_world.launch leaves its include of rrbot_control.launch commented out.

determinism.notes: Event-driven advertisement/publication recording with no PID control, physics step, controller timing or wall-clock pacing; placeholder command records do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free rosbridge contract stand-in (no Gazebo physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it records advertise and publish messages for the two declared command topics and runs no Gazebo, gazebo_ros_control, controller_manager, PID, physics, ROS graph or wall-clock loop
the command records are placeholders and do not move a simulated joint; a live run needs the operator's Gazebo, gazebo_ros_control and rosbridge deployment

the pinned clone names /rrbot/joint_states, /rrbot/laser/scan and /rrbot/camera1/image_raw but does not declare their message types; the SDK requires an explicit type binding, so the joint-state, laser and camera observations are NOT COVERED rather than guessed
no source-backed stop, pause, controller switch or safe-state action is declared; the runtime software latch is not an independent stop and does not interrupt the controllers or the world
the URDF declares both joints continuous, so the clone states no joint travel bound; the operator overlay must supply every joint envelope before a command is admitted
the Gazebo product launch, physics parameters, controller gains, joint state, laser, camera, TF, clock, RViz and controller_manager services are out of scope
no ROS graph, Gazebo process or hardware is contacted; a live run needs the operator's ROS 1 graph and rosbridge endpoint

rrbot_rqt.launch opens rqt_gui with a saved publisher for /rrbot/joint1_position_controller/command (disabled, rate 100, data sin(i/100)); enabled in the GUI it competes with this package and keeps moving joint1 while MHS is latched
rrbot_world.launch does not start the controllers (its rrbot_control.launch include is commented out); until rrbot_control.launch runs, the command topics have no subscriber and a publication is lost

licence: the README states GPL-3.0, the rrbot_control, rrbot_description and rrbot_gazebo manifests declare BSD and gazebo_tutorials declares TODO; the card says NOASSERTION and publish_review required

operator_required.name: set_joint1_position
operator_required.reason: rrbot.xacro declares joint1 as a continuous joint with no travel bound, and rrbot_control.yaml declares PID gains but no position limit; the site supplies the joint1 envelope

operator_required.name: set_joint2_position
operator_required.reason: rrbot.xacro declares joint2 as a continuous joint with no travel bound, and rrbot_control.yaml declares PID gains but no position limit; the site supplies the joint2 envelope

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop exists in the pinned clone: both control endpoints are fire-and-forget std_msgs/Float64 publications, and the clone declares no pause, stop, controller-switch, reset or safe-state service or action. A zero-position publication is transmission only. The runtime software latch refuses new commands but cannot interrupt the external controllers or Gazebo, so a stock e-stop reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED and this package does not claim a stopped state.
